gloss: earth and stone; soil and rocks; debris

definitions.gloss: earth and stone; soil and rocks; debris
definitions.explanation: A collective term for soil, dirt, and rocks. Frequently appears in disaster-related contexts, particularly regarding landslides and mudflows, as well as in construction and geology.

examples.japanese: ⟦{大雨|おおあめ}→大雨：03015_ooame⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{土石|どせき}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{崩|くず}れた→崩れる：04248_kuzureru⟧。
examples.english: Earth and rocks collapsed due to heavy rain.

examples.japanese: {土石流|どせきりゅう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{危険|きけん}→危険：01141_kiken⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧⟦{地域|ちいき}→地域：01461_chiiki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{住|す}んでいる→住む：00673_sumu⟧。
examples.english: I live in an area at risk of mudflows.

examples.japanese: ⟦{工事|こうじ}{現場|げんば}→工事現場：26202_koujigenba⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{大量|たいりょう}→大量：03112_tairyou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{土石|どせき}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{運|はこ}び{出|だ}された→運び出す：30531_hakobidasu⟧。
examples.english: A large amount of earth and stone was hauled from the construction site.

notes:
A paired compound of {土|ど} (earth, soil) and {石|せき} (stone, rock). Most commonly encountered in the compound {土石流|どせきりゅう} (mudflow, debris flow), which is a major natural disaster concern in mountainous Japan. Appears frequently in weather warnings and disaster reports.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {土石流|どせきりゅう}: mudflow, debris flow
- {土石|どせき}{崩|くず}れ: collapse of earth and stone
- {土石|どせき}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{撤去|てっきょ}→撤去：14729_tekkyo⟧: removal of earth and stone
- {土石|どせき}⟦{災害|さいがい}→災害：09636_saigai⟧: earth and rock disaster

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{土砂|どしゃ}→土砂：17540_dosha⟧: earth and sand — also used in disaster contexts (⟦{土砂|どしゃ}{崩|くず}れ→土砂崩れ：09257_doshakuzure⟧, ⟦{土砂|どしゃ}→土砂：17540_dosha⟧⟦{災害|さいがい}→災害：09636_saigai⟧) but emphasizes finer sediment rather than rocks
- ⟦{岩石|がんせき}→岩石：20502_ganseki⟧: rock — refers specifically to rocks and geological formations
- ⟦{瓦礫|がれき}→瓦礫：30524_gareki⟧: rubble, debris — broken fragments, especially from destroyed buildings
